To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the coupling of conduction and valence bands in a two-band superlattice leads to a splitting of minibands and to a reduction of the miniband width, and that these effects increase with the number of bands in the semiconductor host material.
1) The coupling of bands in two-band semiconductors leads to the formation of minibands, which are different from the minibands formed in one-band superlattices.

(1) the coupling between the conduction and valence band leads to a significant change of the miniband width for high minibands; (2) the electron and hole minibands are not symmetric with respect to the center of the Brillouin zone; (3) the miniband width is not a monotonous function of the miniband index; (4) the miniband widths for electrons and holes can be very different.

electron dynamics in semiconductor superlattics.
the electronic properties of two-band superlattices.
the dynamics of electrons in a two-band, sawtooth superlattice.

the band coupling is a significant effect in two-band semiconductor sawtooth superlattice, especially for the second miniband, which is of practical interest.

The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the case of sawtooth superlattice with a large number of doped sheets, the coupling between the two bands of the host semiconductor is strong enough to give rise to a significant difference between the one-band and two-band models.
